headline: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label Flaws
standfirst: CISA's KEV update leads a day of compromised or exposed management infrastructure: Check Point management servers at 22 organizations, a 9.8 vCenter authentication bypass in a 23-flaw VMware batch, and an Azure APIM hunt for tokens and secrets. Radware's exposed API, a no-login WHMCS SQL injection, KEPCO's 1.5 million-person breach and an Iran-aligned group's IPFS-backed backdoor fill out the picture.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added two flaws to its KEV catalog, one affecting N-able MailAssure and one affecting MONAI Label, citing evidence of active exploitation [[s38]]. The supplied enriched record covers CVE-2026-134624, a Critical 9.3 SSRF (CWE-918) in MailAssure's LDAP synchronisation connection check; NVD says an authenticated API user can make the server connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine reachability and send crafted data to internal services, with versions before 20261121.1943 affected. CISA's required action calls for vendor mitigations under BOD 26-04, or discontinuing use where mitigations are unavailable; that is a federal compliance path, not a universal deadline. The MONAI Label flaw's CVE and severity were not supplied. Separately, threat actors exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise two dozen Check Point Security management servers at 22 organizations in an ongoing campaign [[s13]]. The excerpt does not name the CVEs or actor. Analysis: the management plane is the issue — compromising security infrastructure turns it into an intrusion path.

## Vulnerabilities

Broadcom patched 23 vulnerabilities across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion and Avi Load Balancer, including CVE-2026-123903, a 9.8 authentication bypass in VMware Directory Service ("vmdir") [[s24]]. The supplied data records knownExploited as false and no NVD record; that is a KEV catalog miss, not proof that exploitation has not occurred. Analysis: a 9.8 directory-service authentication bypass in vCenter warrants urgent virtualization admin review, though the excerpt truncates the attacker prerequisites. Norway's NSM disclosed an Azure API Management flaw that affected multiple businesses, including Equinor and Skagerak Energi; it said an unknown actor has actively looked for access tokens, secrets and named values in APIM, and Microsoft has fixed the flaw [[s33]]. The excerpt leaves the intrusion path unresolved. Analysis: token and secret hunting is the impact to prioritize. WHMCS disclosed a SQL injection that needs no login and could let anyone on the internet retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from an installation's database, alongside two other flaws that require a logged-in client [[s36]]. Analysis: for hosting providers, billing-platform exposure reaches both client data and admin credential material.

## Breaches

Radware says attackers accessed some customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF management API left exposed online [[s7]]. The excerpt does not give the number of customers or the exposure window. Analysis: cloud keys turn a vendor-side API exposure into downstream customer risk. KEPCO suffered a breach affecting 1.5 million people, with personal information stolen from its customer portal and supplier relationship management platform [[s32]]. Analysis: the supplier-system element broadens the incident beyond retail customers; the excerpt does not describe the data types further.

## Research

The group described as Volant Manticore, a previously undocumented Iran-aligned espionage group, targeted telecommunications companies, airlines and critical infrastructure in Cyprus [[s9]]. Its KuboShell backdoor uses IPFS for command-and-control and deploys Homa, described as a post-compromise framework and a reimplementation of an unspecified framework. Analysis: IPFS-based C2 is a resilience choice that can complicate static blocking, but the supplied text does not detail its operational security.

selected.excerpt: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday added two flaws impacting N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. The critical vulnerabilities are listed below - CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in N-able MailAssure's LDAP

kev.vulnerabilityName: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the LDAP synchronization connection check that allows an authenticated API user to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) before 20261121.1943 does not restrict the destination of the LDAP synchronisation connection check performed when a relay is configured. An authenticated API user can cause the server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.

selected.angle: CISA KEV confirmation of active exploitation in N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label makes immediate patching the day's top priority.

A stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler of the
Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controller allows remote attackers to send specially

and hypothetically potential arbitrary code execution with webserver privileges.
Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.
